title: Assumed reading error limits kept four joint ozone and dry-air contrasts above zero in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We tested whether bounded reading errors permit reversal of joint high-ozone and dry-air exposure contrasts in a wildflower experiment. We used 1,464 hourly records in August and September 2021 in North Wales. At assumed limits of 0.5 C, 3 relative humidity percentage points and 5 ppb ozone per reading, all four monthly heated-minus-ambient contrasts at the 80 and 110 ppb targets stayed positive. Their lower limits were 2.42 to 7.64 percentage points. Doubling all limits permitted zero or negative contrasts in three of four tests. We give sharp bounds under unrestricted errors within physical reading intervals. The source gives no calibration error estimates, so these are conditional sensitivity results. Shared ambient weather, possible source gap filling, one chamber per treatment and one site-year limit inference. The months are not independent regional or experimental replications. No plant response, absorbed ozone or climate trend was tested. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Sharp joint-hour contrast bounds under assumed bounded reading errors. Solid lines are lower bounds; dotted lines are upper bounds. The scale is an assumption, not measured sensor accuracy.
